summary: Round-1 major is genuinely closed — re-verified independently, not on the author's word. The in-process-marker mutant (module-global dict keyed on today's date replacing both repo calls in job()) is now killed by test_a_marker_from_an_earlier_start_suppresses_the_first_tick AND by test_a_delivered_ping_is_recorded_where_a_restart_will_find_it, each run ALONE in its own pytest process, so neither kill depends on cross-test pollution. All three round-1 minors are closed too: the frozen 00:05 UTC boundary kills the rolling-24h mutant at every wall-clock time (verified across seven frozen times of day and under TZ=Europe/Moscow), and the exact-24h case is off the boundary. Full suite green: 1970 passed, 518 subtests. What remains is a coverage asymmetry, not a false-confidence problem: of the four defensive changes this increment makes, two are pinned by mutation and two are not. The mark_dry_spell_pinged() try/except in job() — the half of round-1 finding #4 that was not addressed — survives deletion untouched by all ten tests, and its documented failure mode is skipping _record_heartbeat() and looking like a dead tick to the external watchdog. The (ValueError, TypeError) widening of the shared _parse_dt_tolerant survives reversion too, although test_unreadable_marker_does_not_suppress's docstring states it is the case that pins it; the dry-spell gate's blanket except masks it completely, while the real exposure is is_hold_cap_ping_rate_limited(), which raises TypeError on a BLOB row with the fix reverted. Answering the four questions directly: (1) yes, both boundary tests kill the mutant in isolation; (2) the non-UTC-offset case IS discriminating (kills the .date()-without-normalise mutant), the future-marker case is NOT — deleting the whole future guard leaves every test green, because under a calendar-day rule the guard cannot change a return value; (3) yes, test_an_unreadable_gate_still_lets_the_alarm_through exercises the new try/except specifically — removing the guard drops the count to 0 and flipping its default to fail-closed also drops it to 0, so the test pins the direction and not merely the absence of a traceback; (4) two tests still flip, both spurious REDs rather than silent greens, in a measured ~1 s window per day each.

findings.issue: The increment adds TWO guards inside the dry-spell block and round 2 tested only one. Round-1 finding #4 named both — «Also untested: mark_dry_spell_pinged() raising after a successful send» — and the write-side half was not picked up. Verified by mutation: deleting the try/except around pending_repo.mark_dry_spell_pinged() so the exception propagates leaves ALL TEN new tests green when each is run in isolation (M14 — nothing injects a fault into the marking call anywhere in the suite; the only other reference to mark_dry_spell_pinged in tests/ is the happy path at tests/test_pending_articles_repo.py:2565). The guard's own comment states the consequence it prevents: letting it raise «would skip `_record_heartbeat()` below and look like a dead tick to the watchdog» — i.e. the [E017] bookkeeping failing would silence the external uptime.yml watchdog's liveness signal, which is a strictly worse outcome than the duplicate ping the guard trades for. That is the same «монитоинг не должен ломать тик» guarantee the sibling gate guard now has a test for, and it is currently held by a comment alone. The asymmetry also makes the block read as if both paths were considered and only one mattered.
findings.recommendation: Add one test in TestDrySpellAlert, mirroring the shape of test_an_unreadable_gate_still_lets_the_alarm_through so the pair reads as one decision: def test_a_failed_marker_write_does_not_break_the_tick(self, mock_admin, _mock_sleep): self._seed_silence(); with patch.object(news_bot.pending_repo, 'mark_dry_spell_pinged', side_effect=sqlite3.OperationalError('disk I/O error')): with patch.object(news_bot, '_record_heartbeat') as mock_hb: self._run_job(). Three assertions, each pinning a distinct claim in the comment: assertEqual(self._e017_count(mock_admin), 1) — the send itself is unaffected; assertTrue(mock_hb.called, 'a failed marker write must not cost the tick its heartbeat — the watchdog reads it as a dead container') — this is the assertion that kills the mutant and the one the comment actually promises; and, for the documented «costs at most one duplicate ping tomorrow», a second self._run_job() outside the patch asserting the count reaches 2 (the day went unmarked, so the next tick re-pings). Only the one repo function is mocked; keep the real sqlite DB. Re-verify with the mutant above (delete the try/except, keep the bare call) — the new test must fail alone.

findings.issue: The BLOB and int cases added to the garbage set do not pin the change they are documented as pinning. The test's docstring says «The BLOB case is not hypothetical padding: ... `fromisoformat` answers a non-str with TypeError rather than ValueError — which used to escape the gate and disable [E017] until someone found the row», but reverting `except (ValueError, TypeError)` to `except ValueError` leaves all ten new tests green in isolation (M6). The reason is structural: is_dry_spell_ping_rate_limited() wraps its whole body in a blanket `except Exception: return False`, so within THIS gate the TypeError is swallowed either way and the two implementations are behaviourally identical. That is a litmus failure against the line the test names, and it matters because the widening is a change to a SHARED helper with three call sites. Direct probe: with the fix reverted, seeding key='hold_cap_last_pinged_at' with sqlite3.Binary(b'\x00\x01') makes is_hold_cap_ping_rate_limited(6) RAISE TypeError('fromisoformat: argument must be str'), where the shipped code returns False — that gate has no blanket except (pending_articles_repo.py:712-719), so the [E038] path is where the fix actually does work, and nothing in the suite covers it. So the increment can be silently reverted on this point while the findings log records it as applied and verified.
findings.recommendation: Pin it where the behaviour actually differs, one assertion, no new class. Either (a) at the helper — a direct case in the existing repo test file: self.assertIsNone(pending_articles_repo._parse_dt_tolerant(sqlite3.Binary(b'\x00\x01'), 'k')) and the same for 12345, which fails with TypeError the moment the tuple is narrowed; or (b) at the caller that has no blanket except, which is the stronger test because it names the consequence: add the BLOB and int values to TestHoldCapPingRateLimit's corrupt-value case and assert is_hold_cap_ping_rate_limited(6) returns False rather than raising. Prefer (b), or do both — (b) alone is enough to kill the mutant. Keep the BLOB/int entries in the dry-spell garbage set as they are, but correct that docstring: within this gate they exercise the blanket except, not the parser, and claiming otherwise is what made the gap invisible. Re-verify by narrowing the tuple back to `except ValueError:` — the new assertion must fail alone.

findings.issue: Both restart-dimension tests still flip when UTC midnight falls mid-test, and round 1's recommendation to freeze the job-level tests was applied only to the repo-level one. Measured, not inferred: driving the clock with freeze_time(..., tick=True) from a range of start offsets and running each test 39 times, test_a_marker_from_an_earlier_start_suppresses_the_first_tick fails whenever midnight lands 0.1–1.1 s after the test starts (the marker is written on the old date, the gate reads on the new one → 1 != 0), and test_restarts_within_one_day_ping_once fails whenever it lands 0.8–2.0 s in (tick 1 marks the old date, a later tick re-pings on the new one → 2 != 1). That is roughly a 1 s window per test per day. Both are spurious REDS, not silent greens, so no false confidence — but they are the two tests carrying the restart criterion, i.e. exactly the ones an operator would re-run and mistrust after an unexplained CI failure. The remaining eight tests were clean across the same sweep and across seven frozen times of day (00:00:00.2, 00:05, 06:00, 12:00, 23:30, 23:55, 23:59:59.5); test_marking_suppresses_the_rest_of_the_day has the same shape but a sub-millisecond window, too narrow to be worth touching.
findings.recommendation: Decorate both with @freeze_time, as TestDrySpellPingRateLimit.test_gate_follows_the_calendar_day already is — freezegun is a dev dep and the import is already in the sibling file. Put the instant mid-day rather than near a boundary, since neither test is about the boundary: @freeze_time('2026-08-18 12:00:00') on each. Nothing else changes — _seed_silence() computes its 5-day-old timestamp from the frozen now, and the marker seeded at the frozen now stays on the frozen date. One caveat found while testing this: freezegun must not be active while tests/test_job_distributed_publish.py is first imported (a class in the import chain subclasses datetime and hits a metaclass conflict under FakeDatetime), which the decorator form avoids since import happens at collection. Verify with the same tick=True sweep — after freezing, no start offset should produce a failure.

findings.issue: Answering the question directly: the non-UTC-offset case is discriminating, the future-marker case is not. The offset case earns its place — replacing `marked = last.astimezone(timezone.utc).date()` with `last.date()` fails it (M3), and it is the only case that does. The future case does not: deleting the entire `if marked > today:` block — nine lines and a WARNING — leaves every one of the ten tests green (M4). The reason is that the guard cannot change a return value under a calendar-day rule: if marked > today then `marked == today` is already False, so the guard's only observable effect is the log line, and the test asserts only the return value. What the case DOES kill is a `return marked >= today` variant (M5), i.e. an implementation that honours a future marker — a plausible enough shape to be worth keeping. But it should not be recorded as pinning the new production code, because it does not: the guard is currently untestable through its return value. A second, smaller instance of the same pattern: dropping the `if last.tzinfo is None: last = last.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` fill-in (M10) also leaves everything green, and it cannot be pinned from this suite at all — the runner's TZ is UTC while prod runs Europe/Moscow, so a naive-value case would pass either way locally and only diverge in the container.
findings.recommendation: Pick one of two, not both. (a) Keep the guard and assert its only observable effect, which also documents WHY it exists: with self.assertLogs('pending_articles_repo', level='WARNING') as cm: self._store('2026-08-19T00:01:00+00:00'); self.assertFalse(pending_articles_repo.is_dry_spell_ping_rate_limited()); self.assertTrue(any('future-dated' in m for m in cm.output), 'a future-dated marker must be reported — it can never be overwritten, so a silent False hides a clock fault'). This kills M4 and keeps the M5 kill. Note the case then needs lifting out of the shared subTest loop, since the other five cases log nothing. (b) If the log is not considered worth an assertion, drop the guard from production as behaviourally inert under a calendar-day gate and keep the test case as-is guarding against `>=` — but then say so in the docstring instead of calling it new behaviour. For the naive fill-in: leave it, and record in the increment notes that only mark_dry_spell_pinged() ever writes this key and it always writes an aware ISO string, so the branch is reachable only via a hand-edited row — otherwise the next reviewer re-derives the same dead end. Re-verify (a) by deleting the `if marked > today:` block; the new assertion must fail alone.
